forces.title: Longer Trade Routes Boost Shipping Demand and Rates
forces.description: Global trade remaining resilient and disruptions creating longer trade routes are benefiting shipping companies. This extends sailing distances, supporting demand for shipping services and contributing to better-than-expected performance in the maritime sector, especially for globally active Dutch firms. This trend provides a crucial advantage for revenue generation.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Energy Transition and AI Infrastructure Drive Freight Demand
forces.description: Investments in the energy transition and AI infrastructure are creating additional freight demand globally. This development is expected to particularly benefit globally active shipping companies and Dutch ports, as increased trade associated with these infrastructure projects translates into higher volumes for maritime transport services, supporting future growth.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Weather Disruptions Support Freight Rates
forces.description: Global supply chains are increasingly affected by geopolitical tensions, protectionism, and extreme weather events. While these factors create operational challenges for the transport sector, they also generate opportunities for logistics providers and, significantly, help support elevated freight rates in maritime shipping, contributing to sector resilience.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Global Trade Growth and Chokepoint Disruptions Drive Shipping Demand
forces.description: Global goods trade continues to grow, particularly with strong export expansion from China, providing a tailwind for shipping. Additionally, disruptions in critical maritime chokepoints like the Red Sea, Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz, and Panama Canal are forcing longer sailing distances, which directly supports and increases demand for shipping services globally.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Low Water Levels Boost Inland Shipping Freight Rates
forces.description: Exceptionally low water levels have once again restricted inland shipping capacity. This leads to loading limitations and tight vessel availability, which has pushed inland freight rates higher. This situation is likely to result in a financially strong year for inland operators in the short term, despite underlying structural issues.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Recurring Low Water Levels Threaten Long-Term Inland Shipping
forces.description: While low water levels currently boost inland shipping freight rates, recurring disruptions are problematic structurally. They may encourage shippers to shift freight from inland waterways to road transport, undermining long-term modal shift ambitions and impacting the sustainability of inland maritime transport as a preferred option for certain goods in the future.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Parcel Levy Shifts Traffic Towards Maritime Transport
forces.description: The introduction of a €3 European parcel levy has significantly affected demand for Chinese parcel volumes. Consequently, part of this traffic is shifting towards consolidated shipments and maritime transport, followed by European fulfilment-centre distribution. This represents a new, albeit smaller, demand source for the shipping sector, contributing to its volumes.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Maritime Chokepoint Disruptions Threaten Global Shipping Stability
forces.description: Maritime chokepoints are vulnerable to geopolitical tensions, climate events, and technological threats (drones, missiles, GPS jamming). Disruptions cause carriers to suspend services, fragment shipping patterns, and sharply increase freight and insurance costs. Rerouting adds significant distance, time, and cost, reducing effective vessel capacity and driving up bidding rates, impacting shipping profitability and reliability.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: Technology Enables Cheaper Disruption of Commercial Shipping
forces.description: Technology is making disruption easier and less expensive for state and nonstate actors. Low-cost aerial and surface drones, precision missiles, GPS jamming, and AIS spoofing have emerged as significant threats to commercial shipping. This represents a structural shift in maritime security, increasing the operational risks and potential for cost escalation for shipping companies.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: Rerouting and Longer Voyages Increase Shipping Costs and Rates
forces.description: When chokepoints are disrupted, ships reroute, adding thousands of kilometers and weeks to voyages (e.g., Gibraltar +85%, Panama +47%, Suez +46%). These longer distances tie up vessels, reducing effective capacity and leading to fewer round trips and containers moved per month. This tightens shipping capacity, pushing freight rates higher.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: Supply Chain Diversification Away from Single Chokepoints
forces.description: Following prolonged disruptions, many countries are actively working to reduce their exposure to single maritime chokepoints. This involves diversifying supply chains, de-concentrating reliance on specific routes, and reducing dependence on imported energy, labor, and technology. This trend represents a structural shift in global trade routes and logistics planning for shippers.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: Businesses Implement Proactive Chokepoint Risk Mitigation Strategies
forces.description: Companies are now proactively identifying and estimating their exposure to maritime chokepoints through supply chain mapping and scenario stress-testing, often using AI tools like digital twins. Mitigation measures include diversifying suppliers across origins and routes, building inventory buffers, and localizing production, fundamentally reshaping global logistics and supply chain resilience.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: Fuel Prices, Carbon Taxes, and Decarbonization Costs Burden Irish Transport
forces.description: Ireland's transport sector, including maritime, faces persistent cost pressures from elevated fuel prices and rising carbon taxes. The need for continuous investment in lower-emission fleets to meet EU climate requirements further adds to operational expenses. These escalating costs significantly impact the profitability and financial resilience of transport operators.

forces.title: AI-Driven Pricing Strategies Offer Significant Margin Growth for Logistics
forces.description: Advanced analytics and maturing AI technology are dramatically lowering barriers to implementing sophisticated pricing strategies across logistics subsectors, including ocean shipping. Companies that pinpoint willingness to pay, digitize deal reviews, use price to shape networks, and automate price execution can achieve 20% faster annual price growth and top-quartile EBIT growth by leveraging data for nuanced differentiation and dynamic adjustments.

forces.title: Middle East Conflict Drives Freight Surcharges and Rate Increases
forces.description: The ongoing Middle East conflict is leading to freight and logistics surcharges and energy price hikes for shipping operators. This has resulted in higher rates on key trade routes like Transpacific and Asia-Europe, as reflected by the Drewry World Container Price Index. The impact varies significantly based on specific routes, carriers, and existing shipping agreements.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Energy Price Hikes and Supply Chain Delays Affect Shipping
forces.description: Shipping operators are experiencing significant headwinds from energy price hikes and widespread supply chain delays, exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. While some routes see rate increases, the overall rise in operational costs, particularly fuel, and the inefficiencies caused by delays place considerable pressure on profitability and operational continuity across the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Dutch Maritime Shipping resilient with unexpected strong performance
viewpoints.description: The Dutch transport and logistics sector is experiencing moderate growth, partly driven by globally active maritime shipping performing better than anticipated in 2026. Shipping companies are specifically benefiting from extended trade routes, contributing to resilience amidst global uncertainties and rising costs. International markets are expected to offer less support in 2027, but global trade remains robust.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Dutch shipping benefits from global trade growth despite port pressure
viewpoints.description: Globally active Dutch shipping companies are benefiting from continued global trade growth, which has remained near 5% in H1 2026, driven by China's exports. Despite port throughput and container volumes being under pressure, disruptions in key maritime chokepoints are maintaining longer sailing distances. This supports demand for shipping services, aiding the sector's performance.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Maritime chokepoints are a growing, complex source of global trade disruption
viewpoints.description: Global businesses face increasing disruption from maritime chokepoints, which carry 80% of world trade by volume. Geopolitical tensions, climate issues, and technological threats (drones, missiles, GPS jamming) make these waterways vulnerable. Disruptions lead to rerouting, increased distances, higher freight and insurance costs, reduced effective shipping capacity, and ripple effects across supply chains.
viewpoints.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

viewpoints.title: Irish transport sector stable but faces headwinds from costs and weak demand
viewpoints.description: Ireland's transport sector, including maritime, operates in a stable environment, supported by trade flows and economic activity. However, growth is constrained by weaker external demand and geopolitical uncertainty. Persistent cost pressures from elevated fuel prices, rising carbon taxes, and investment in lower-emission fleets, along with driver shortages, are impacting capacity and profitability.

viewpoints.title: Middle East conflict causes freight surcharges and rising shipping rates
viewpoints.description: The Middle East conflict is significantly impacting shipping operators through freight and logistics surcharges, energy price hikes, and supply chain delays. The Drewry World Container Price Index has seen increases, driven by higher rates on Transpacific and Asia-Europe trade routes, while Transatlantic spot rates remain stable. These dynamics emphasize varied effects based on routes, carriers, and agreements.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

demand_drivers.description: Global trade remains resilient, supported by consumer demand and export expansion from China, benefiting globally active maritime shipping.
Geopolitical disruptions in key maritime chokepoints (Red Sea, Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz, Panama Canal) maintain longer sailing distances, supporting demand for shipping services.
Investments in the energy transition and AI infrastructure are generating additional freight demand globally, benefiting shipping companies.

pnl_drivers.description: Longer trade routes and disruptions contribute to higher freight rates, improving revenue per shipment for shipping companies.
Exceptionally low water levels restrict inland shipping capacity, leading to loading limitations and tight vessel availability, pushing freight rates higher for inland operators.

new_opportunities.description: The introduction of a €3 European parcel levy has affected Chinese parcel volumes, shifting some of this traffic towards consolidated shipments and maritime transport, followed by European fulfilment-centre distribution.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Shift from Parcel to Maritime Transport

market_sizing.methodology: The Dutch transport and logistics sector overall is expected to grow by around 1% in 2026, with globally active aviation and maritime shipping performing better than expected. Growth for the broader sector is forecast to accelerate modestly to around 1.5% in 2027.
market_sizing.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…
